docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Use key vocabulary about the environment and technology.
- Talk about environmental problems and solutions.
- Describe modern technology and its effects on our lives.
- Give your opinion on these topics using useful phrases.

🔍 Warm-up
Two big topics shape our world today: the environment and technology. What is one problem the planet faces? What is one gadget you use every day? This lesson gives you the words to discuss both in English.

I. The environment: key vocabulary
📘 Rule (vocabulary — problems)
- pollution: air pollution, water pollution, noise pollution.
- climate change and global warming: the Earth is getting warmer.
- waste and rubbish (American: garbage / trash).
- deforestation: cutting down forests.
- endangered species: animals in danger of disappearing.
- drought: a long period without rain.

📘 Rule (vocabulary — solutions)
- recycle: use materials again (paper, plastic, glass).
- reduce: use less (less plastic, less energy).
- reuse: use something more than once.
- save energy / save water.
- renewable energy: solar power, wind power.
- protect nature, plant trees, clean beaches.

✏️ Worked examples
- We should recycle plastic bottles.
- Pollution is a serious problem in big cities.
- Solar energy is clean and renewable.

👀 Note (three useful verbs)
The "three R" idea is easy to remember: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. Reduce = use less; Reuse = use again; Recycle = turn into a new product.

II. Talking about problems and solutions
📏 Form (useful structures)
- ... is a big problem because ...
- We should / We must + base verb (advice, obligation).
- We shouldn't waste ...
- If we ..., we will ... (first conditional).

✏️ Worked examples
- Air pollution is a big problem because it makes people ill.
- We should use bikes instead of cars.
- If we recycle more, we will produce less waste.
- We must protect endangered animals.

🛠️ Method: discussing an environmental issue
Step 1 — Name the problem: Plastic waste is harmful.
Step 2 — Explain why: because it pollutes the sea.
Step 3 — Suggest a solution: We should use cloth bags.
Step 4 — Add a result with the first conditional: If we do this, we will save marine life.

III. Technology: key vocabulary
📘 Rule (vocabulary — devices and the internet)
- devices: computer, laptop, tablet, smartphone, screen.
- the internet: website, email, app, social media, online, download, upload.
- actions: to chat, to search, to click, to post, to share, to send a message.
- people: user, developer.

📘 Rule (vocabulary — describing technology)
- Positive: useful, fast, modern, helpful, convenient.
- Negative: expensive, addictive, harmful, dangerous.

✏️ Worked examples
- I use a laptop to do my homework.
- Social media helps us stay in touch with friends.
- Many students spend too much time on their smartphones.

IV. The effects of technology
📘 Rule (advantages and disadvantages)
Technology has good and bad sides. Learn to present both.
📏 Useful phrases
- One advantage of ... is that ...
- On the other hand, ...
- However, ...
- Some people think ... but others believe ...
✏️ Worked examples
- One advantage of the internet is that it gives us a lot of information.
- On the other hand, spending too much time online can be bad for our health.
- Smartphones are useful, however they can be addictive.

🛠️ Method: giving a balanced opinion
Step 1 — State an advantage: The internet helps us learn.
Step 2 — Add a disadvantage with a contrast word: However, it can waste our time.
Step 3 — Give your personal opinion: In my opinion, we should use it wisely.

✏️ Worked paragraph
Technology and the environment are connected. Modern devices such as smartphones and computers make our lives easier and help us communicate. However, producing them uses a lot of energy and creates electronic waste. In my opinion, we should use technology carefully and recycle old devices. If everyone reduces waste and saves energy, we will protect our planet for the future.

👀 Note (giving opinions politely)
Useful opinion phrases: I think that ..., In my opinion, ..., I believe ..., I agree / I disagree, It seems to me that ...

⚠️ Common mistakes
1. Uncountable nouns: informations, technologies (as "gadgets"), pollutions → information, technology, pollution (usually uncountable).
2. "should" + base verb only: We should to recycle → We should recycle.
3. Spelling: enviroment → environment; tecnology → technology.
4. Mixing "waste" (rubbish or to use badly) with "waist" (part of the body).

⭐ Recap
- Environment words: pollution, climate change, waste, recycle, reduce, reuse, renewable energy.
- Technology words: device, internet, app, social media, download, user.
- Use "should / must" for advice and the first conditional for results.
- Present balanced opinions with "one advantage ... however ... in my opinion".

📘 Language bank
Environment: pollution, climate change, global warming, waste, recycle, reduce, reuse, renewable energy, protect, endangered species.
Technology: computer, laptop, smartphone, tablet, internet, website, app, social media, download, online, user.
Opinion phrases: I think that ..., In my opinion, ..., One advantage is ..., However, ..., On the other hand, ...
Useful sentences: Pollution is a serious problem. / We should recycle more. / If we save energy, we will help the planet. / The internet is useful but it can be addictive. / In my opinion, we must protect nature.

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Environment or Technology? Sort these words.
recycle, smartphone, pollution, download, deforestation, app, renewable energy, website, waste, social media.
Environment: ______
Technology: ______

Exercise 2 — Complete with a word from the lesson.
1. We should ______ plastic bottles instead of throwing them away.
2. Solar and wind power are types of ______ energy.
3. Air ______ makes people ill in big cities.
4. Many people spend hours on ______ media every day.

Exercise 3 — Give a balanced opinion. Complete the sentences.
1. One advantage of the internet is that ______ .
2. However, ______ .
3. In my opinion, ______ .

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: Environment: recycle, pollution, deforestation, renewable energy, waste. Technology: smartphone, download, app, website, social media.
Exercise 2: 1. recycle 2. renewable 3. pollution 4. social.

🗣️ Speaking task
Hold a mini-debate: "Is technology good or bad for young people?" One group gives advantages, the other gives disadvantages. Use "One advantage is...", "On the other hand...", "In my opinion...".

👀 Extra note
Two structures make you sound advanced on these topics:
1. Advice and obligation: We SHOULD recycle. We MUST protect nature (should/must + base verb).
2. Cause and result: If we save energy, we WILL help the planet (first conditional).
Watch the spelling of two key words: environment and technology.

📋 Summary
- Environment problems: pollution, climate change/global warming, waste, deforestation, endangered species, drought.
- Environment solutions: the 3 Rs (reduce, reuse, recycle), save energy/water, renewable energy, protect nature.
- Useful structures: We should/must + base verb (advice/obligation); If we ..., we will ... (first conditional for results).
- Technology devices: computer, laptop, tablet, smartphone; internet actions: chat, search, click, post, share, download, upload.
- Describing technology: positive (useful, fast, convenient) vs negative (expensive, addictive, harmful).
- Balanced opinion structure: One advantage of ... is that ... / On the other hand, ... / However, ... / In my opinion, ...
- Opinion phrases: I think that ..., I believe ..., I agree/disagree, It seems to me that ...
- Common mistakes: "information/technology/pollution" are usually uncountable (no plural -s); "should to" is wrong, use "should + base verb".
- Watch the spelling of "environment" and "technology" — both are frequently misspelled.
